summary: Discovery focused on cost/unit economics across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments. Novus needs to understand per-token pricing, batching and KV/prefix caching levers, expected unit costs at their traffic profile, and budget constraints for a pilot. Redwood AE/SE outlined tradeoffs (latency vs cost), batching strategies, caching benefits, and recommended a benchmark pilot plus security docs for procurement.
topics: Per-token pricing for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private
transcript: [00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining - this is Jordan from Redwood, AE on the account. Priya's our solutions engineer, she'll handle the technical bits. How's everyone doing?
[00:12] Ethan: Good, thanks. Busy week but excited to dig in, we want to understand cost implications before we push to a pilot.

[00:20] Priya: Great - high level today we'll cover hosted vs dedicated vs private, how per-token pricing maps to batching/caching, and then go through a rough cost model based on the traffic you shared earlier. Any must-cover items?

[00:30] Maria: Security and data residency are big for us - but primarily we're trying to keep unit costs under our current benchmark which is about $0.0008 per 1k tokens effective, so that is kind of the constraint.

[00:45] Jordan: Got it. Let's walk through a simple example. For Redwood hosted our list price for standard open models starts around $X per 1k input tokens / $Y per 1k output tokens - I'll send the exact sheet after - but the key levers that change your effective cost are batching, prefix/KV caching, and model quantization. Priya will explain latency tradeoffs.

[01:10] Priya: Quick note on batching: if you have concurrent low-latency requests, some batching can bundle requests within a small window to amortize GPU work. For throughput-oriented paths we often see 2-3x token-cost reduction versus pure single-request serving. But batching can add a few tens to 100s of ms depending on your SLOs and request variance.

[01:40] Daniel: We're latency-sensitive for our live scoring, target p95 ~250ms. So big batching windows are a no-go for those paths. But we do have background tasks and bulk reranks where latency can be higher.

[01:55] Priya: Exactly - most customers split policy: Hosted for low-friction & bursty needs, Dedicated for predictable throughput on production low-latency paths, Private for strict data residency/compliance. For Dedicated you can reserve a GPU pool which reduces per-token unit cost and avoids multi-tenant tail contention.
[02:15] Ethan: Curious about caching - you mentioned prefix/KV cache, how effective is that for our use case? We have a lot of repeated context across requests due to templates and user metadata.

[02:27] Priya: KV cache helps when you have repeated prefixes - we maintain a session-level KV cache so repeated context tokens don't re-execute attention layers; effective token cost reduction depends on how much of the prompt is prefix vs fresh. In practice, for templated prompts we see 30-60% token savings on the model side. Also we have automatic prefix caching that can work at the routing layer for identical prefixes across users.
[02:55] Maria: That 30-60% range would be huge. Is that available on Hosted? Any extra ops?

[03:05] Jordan: Yes Hosted has prefix/KV caching for supported models; we can enable it per-route. There's no separate license for caching on Hosted. On Dedicated/Private you have more control (and can tune cache sizes), which can improve savings further for heavy session workloads.
[03:24] Ethan: How about quantization - can we drop to 4-bit model variants and what's the impact on quality vs cost?

[03:32] Priya: We support multiple quantization profiles. Moving to aggressive quantization (e.g., Q4) reduces GPU memory and per-token FLOPs which translates to lower unit cost - sometimes up to 30-40% lower. But it depends on your quality tolerance. We recommend running eval prompts (you can share a sample set) and we'll show quality regressions per model/quant profile.

[03:55] Daniel: So to summarize, the main knobs are batching (temporal/window based), caching (prefix/KV), and quantization/model variant. Also Dedicated gives predictable throughput and lower unit cost if we can commit. Correct?
[04:07] Priya: That's right. Also routing policies - you can route non-critical requests to cheaper model variants or a cheaper region to save cost without affecting critical paths.

[04:18] Jordan: On pricing: for Hosted we quote per-token rates (input/output) with tiers as you scale. For Dedicated we move to a capacity-reservation model: monthly commit for GPUs plus a lower per-token or vCPU charge depending on the billing model. Private is license+support and you run on your infra so unit economics depend on your hardware but we provide expectation sheets and pilot-run metrics.

[04:43] Maria: Can you show us a quick back-of-envelope with numbers? Our current baseline is 5M tokens/day, 70% input, 30% output average lengths 30 tokens input / 150 tokens output. That yields X cost now, we want to see Redwood numbers.

[04:58] Priya: Sure - rough calc: 5M tokens/day * 30-day = 150M tokens/month. With Hosted baseline per-1k-token price at $0.50 per 1k tokens (example) that'd be $75k/month before savings. But with batching and caching you might reduce effective tokens by 30-50% depending on workload, and Dedicated commitments could shave another 20-30% from unit cost. We'll run your exact numbers in the model and return a spreadsheet.

[05:30] Ethan: That $75k raw number is helpful to ground things. Our budget for pilot is more like $10k/mo, so we need a plan that's within that for an initial experiment - maybe focus on background batch jobs and a small set of low-latency endpoints.

[05:45] Jordan: Yes many customers start with a narrow pilot: route non-critical use-cases to hosted with caching and batch windows, or use Dedicated burst capacity for predictable tests. We'll propose a pilot that fits $10k/mo and shows regression/quality metrics.
[06:02] Daniel: Procurement question - for Dedicated or Private we need SOC2 reports, SSO/SAML integrations, KMS support and audit logs. Any blockers?

[06:12] Jordan: We have SOC2 Type II, SAML/SSO, RBAC, and KMS integrations - we'll send security pack. Private deployments give full control over KMS/HSM. We'll attach our compliance docs in the follow-up.
[06:26] Maria: About latency - for p95 250ms, what's feasible on Dedicated vs Hosted?

[06:33] Priya: Hosted can meet 250ms p95 for many shorter-context models under typical load, but at high concurrency Dedicated gives better predictable p95 since you're not sharing tail latency. For strict SLOs we recommend Dedicated with a small reserved pool or Private if you need on-prem latency consistency.
[06:50] Ethan: We also have an internal infra team that might prefer Private due to compliance, but initial pilot easier on Hosted. Tradeoffs?

[06:57] Jordan: Hosted = fastest to get started, lowest friction, but multi-tenant. Dedicated = predictable and cost optimized with commitments. Private = max compliance and control but longer setup and ops overhead. We typically do Hosted pilot then move to Dedicated or Private based on procurement.

[07:12] Priya: For the benchmark we recommend a 2-phase run: phase 1 lightweight hosted pilot with your sample prompts (focus on cacheable templates), phase 2 a dedicated/benchmark run where we provision a small GPU pool and run replay tests to measure real token/time cost and p95 latency.
[07:30] Daniel: How long do benchmark runs take and what do we need to provide?

[07:35] Priya: Usually 1-2 weeks to provision and run with a replay harness - you'll provide sample prompts and traffic histogram; we provide results and an annotated cost model. We'll also include quality regressions across model/quant profiles.
[07:46] Jordan: I'll send the pricing sheet and a draft pilot plan. Priya will schedule the deep dive and benchmark. Ethan, Maria, does that align with your timeline?
[07:55] Ethan: Yes, we'd like to kick pilot in mid-April, so the dates you mentioned earlier work.
[08:02] Maria: Ok please include SSO & SOC2 docs in the follow-up so procurement can start opening tickets.
[08:09] Jordan: Will do. Any other questions?
[08:12] Daniel: One more - what's the fallback policy if Dedicated capacity is saturated?

[08:17] Priya: We support smart routing and automatic fallback to compatible model variants or hosted pool; you can set routing policies and capacity thresholds so live traffic can degrade gracefully to a slightly cheaper model or region if needed.
[08:30] Ethan: Nice. That helps with reliability concerns.
[08:34] Jordan: Alright let's recap next steps...

[08:36] Jordan: Next steps - Jordan sends pricing & cost model by 2026-04-09; Priya schedules technical deep dive and benchmark (w/c 2026-04-13); Novus shares sample prompts and traffic histogram by 2026-04-10. We'll include SOC2/KMS/SSO docs in the follow-up email.
[08:58] Maria: Thanks everyone, appreciate the clear plan.
[09:01] Ethan: Thanks, talk soon.
[09:03] Jordan: Thanks all - bye.
